newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum premiums soften, scrap metal firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum premiums soften, scrap metal firmer.

text.p: Spot aluminum business has idled almost to a halt as consumers tidy their books to avoid year end tax on inventory, traders said.

Meanwhile, due to a resurgence in aluminum prices and nascent backwardation on LME, U.S. Midwest delivery premiums have softened by a quarter cent to 4.00 to 4.25 cents for the fourth quarter and into next year, according to merchants.
"It's all because of the slight backwardation on LME - there is nothing going on at the moment," a trader said. "Also people don't want any stocks because of tax problems."
Consumers would have to pay a tax on any metal inventory they hold at the end of December.

With a slight tightness in the January LME contract within the LME cash to three months spread, a third of the contango is lost and people were worried they could not finance their inventory and got rid of it thereby creating some softness, a dealer noted.
Industry analyst Stewart Spector said premiums tend to contract when metal prices rise but then eventually widen if supply and demand conditions become more favorable.
"So far, it's the normal pattern," Spector said.

"There is also a seasonal phenomenom we are going to get into. Prices tend to rise between Thanksgiving and Christmas because by the end of November people have finished what they had to do to clean up their books to year end. Whatever pressures there are, usually come off about now," Spector added.

Aluminum scrap prices have strengthened but the benchmark A380 alloy price of 65 cents per pound - although off the recent lows of about 62 to 63 cents - has failed to recover to the same extent as scrap tags, leaving alloy smelter margins under pressure, a secondary producer said.
"The scrap dealers have the power now, they have the metal and the market is moving up," the producer added.
A merchant said scrap was going to become more expensive as the winter season progressed, especially with early snow hitting parts of the Midwest.
